proposed.text: A storm drain must accommodate a peak discharge of 0.120 m3/s. The rainfall intensity for the design storm is 160 mm/hr, and the runoff coefficient for the catchment is 0.72. What is the minimum drainage area (in hectares) that this discharge represents under the Rational Method?
proposed.rationale: Rational Method in SI units: Q (m3/s) = 0.00278 x C x I (mm/hr) x A (ha), where 0.00278 = 1/3600 x (1 m / 1000 mm) x (10000 m2 / 1 ha). Solving for area: A = Q / (0.00278 x C x I) = 0.120 / (0.00278 x 0.72 x 160) = 0.120 / 0.3201 = 0.375 ha. Correct answer is b. Option a (0.0375 ha) results from a decimal-place error. Option c (3.4 ha) is the original erroneous marked answer (off by a factor of ~9; would imply Q = 1.09 m3/s, not the 0.120 m3/s given in the stem) and reflects omission of the 0.00278 SI conversion constant. Option d (37.5 ha) results from dividing by 0.00278 twice.
proposed.explanation: Storm-drain sizing uses the Rational Method Q = CIA. In SI units (Q in m3/s, I in mm/hr, A in ha), the formula becomes Q = 0.00278 x C x I x A. Rearranging for A: A = 0.120 / (0.00278 x 0.72 x 160) = 0.375 hectares.
